questions.section: Part I: Multiple Choice Questions (40 Marks)
questions.question: 5. Muna finishes a given work in 5 minutes where as Asma finishes the same work in 10 minutes. Which of the following statements is true?
options: a. Muna is more powerful than Asma
b. Muna did more work than Asma
c. Asma is more powerful than Muna
d. Asma did more work than Muna
questions.answer_guide: Same work in less time → greater power (P = W/t).

questions.section: Part II: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
2. The figure shows the forces acting on a car of mass 900 kg. Look at it carefully and then answer the following questions
  a) How can you tell from the diagram that the car is slowing down? (2 marks)
  b) Find the net force acting on the car (2 marks)
  c) What will happen to the motion of the car when drag force becomes equal to motive force? (2 marks)

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 460 170" width="100%" style="max-width:460px" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Car of mass 900 kg with drag 3000 N backwards and thrust 1200 N forwards"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 Z" fill="#111"/></marker></defs><path d="M110,110 L110,80 L160,80 L190,50 L290,50 L320,80 L360,80 L360,110 Z" fill="#eee" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="160" cy="112" r="16" fill="#555" stroke="#111"/><circle cx="310" cy="112" r="16" fill="#555" stroke="#111"/><text x="235" y="100" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">m = 900 kg</text><line x1="100" y1="90" x2="30" y2="90" stroke="#111" stroke-width="4" marker-end="url(#ah)"/><text x="55" y="75" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">DRAG</text><text x="55" y="115" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">3000 N</text><line x1="370" y1="90" x2="440" y2="90" stroke="#111" stroke-width="4" marker-end="url(#ah)"/><text x="410" y="75" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">THRUST</text><text x="410" y="115" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">1200 N</text><line x1="20" y1="128" x2="450" y2="128" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.5"/></svg>
diagram.caption: Car of mass 900 kg: drag force 3000 N acts backwards and thrust 1200 N acts forwards.

questions.answer_guide:
a) The drag (3000 N) is greater than the thrust (1200 N), so the resultant force acts backwards, opposite to the motion, and the car decelerates.
b) Net force = 3000 − 1200 = 1800 N backwards (opposite to the motion). [Deceleration = 1800/900 = 2 m/s².]
c) The forces are balanced (net force = 0), so the car moves at a constant speed (uniform velocity) – it stops slowing down.

questions.section: Part II: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
3. A cyclist of total mass 80 kg is running up a slope as shown in the figure
  a) Which of the points A, B or C, the cyclist has greatest gravitational potential energy? (1 mark)
  b) Work out the GPE of the cyclist at B (2 marks)
  c) If it takes 40 seconds to reach B, calculate the power developed by the cyclist (3 marks)

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 420 200" width="100%" style="max-width:420px" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Hill 10 m high with cyclist at A on the slope, B at the top and C at the bottom"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 Z" fill="#111"/></marker></defs><path d="M20,180 L190,40 L360,180 Z" fill="#ddd" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="105" cy="110" r="6" fill="#111"/><circle cx="190" cy="40" r="6" fill="#111"/><circle cx="345" cy="168" r="6" fill="#111"/><text x="92" y="102" font-size="14" text-anchor="end" font-weight="bold">A</text><text x="190" y="28" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">B</text><text x="345" y="155" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">C</text><line x1="395" y1="40" x2="395" y2="180" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="385" y1="40" x2="405" y2="40" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.5"/><line x1="385" y1="180" x2="405" y2="180" stroke="#111" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="388" y="115" font-size="13" text-anchor="end" font-weight="bold">10 m</text></svg>
diagram.caption: Hill 10 m high: cyclist at A partway up the slope, at B on the top and at C at the bottom of the far side.

questions.answer_guide:
a) B (the highest point).
b) GPE = mgh = 80 × 10 × 10 = 8000 J (taking g = 10 N/kg; 7840 J with g = 9.8).
c) P = work ÷ time = 8000 ÷ 40 = 200 W (196 W with g = 9.8).

4. The figure shows water waves passing through a gap in a barrier
  a) The diagram, draw the trace of the wave as they pass through the gap. (2 marks)
  b) What is the name of this property of waves? Tick one box (1 mark)
     Refraction [ ]
     Diffraction [ ]
  c) If the wavelength of the wave is 3 m and its frequency is 2 Hz, work out the speed of the wave. (3 marks)

questions.answer_guide:
a) After the gap the waves spread out as curved (circular) wavefronts with the same wavelength (spacing) as before.

8. An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 10 cm.
  a) Calculate the position (distance) of the image from the lens. (3 marks)
  b) Find the magnification ratio of the image. (2 marks)
  c) Describe the nature of the image. (1 mark)
questions.answer_guide:
a) 1/f = 1/u + 1/v → 1/v = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → v = 15 cm (on the other side of the lens)
b) m = v/u = 15/30 = 0.5
c) Real, inverted and diminished (half the size of the object).

diagram.caption: Vacuum flask: stopper on top, double walls with shiny silvered surfaces, a vacuum layer between the walls, and liquid inside.

questions.answer_guide:
a) Radiation (shiny surfaces reflect infrared radiation back).
b) Conduction and convection (both need particles; a vacuum has none).
c) Conduction and convection (it stops hot air rising out of the top) – also reduces evaporation.

questions.section: Part II: Structured Questions (60 Marks)
questions.question:
10. The diagram shows a cylinder, balance, liquid and stone arranged as below.
   From the information in the diagram deduce
  a) The mass of the cylinder. (2 marks)
  b) The mass of the liquid. (2 marks)
  c) The mass of the stone. (2 marks)

diagram.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 480 230" width="100%" style="max-width:480px" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Measuring cylinder on a balance: empty 60 g; diagram.caption: Three measuring cylinders on a balance: empty (60 g); with liquid to 20 mL (120 g); with a stone added, level 50 mL (160 g).

questions.answer_guide:
a) 60 g (reading when empty)
b) 120 − 60 = 60 g
c) 160 − 120 = 40 g
[Extra: liquid density = 60/20 = 3 g/cm³; stone volume = 50 − 20 = 30 cm³, density ≈ 1.33 g/cm³.]
